questions.question:
In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

43, 45, 42, 46, 41, 47, ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is:

Each alternate odd place digit is subtracted by 1 each time and each alternate even place digit is added by 1 each time.

i.e. 43 - 1 = 42; 42 - 1 = 41 and 45 + 1 = 46; 46 + 1 = 47

Hence the next missing term is 41 - 1 = **40**

In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

4, 13, 41, 126, 382, ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is:

4 × 3 = 12 + 1 = 13

13 × 3 = 39 + 2 = 41

41 × 3 = 123 + 3 = 126

126 × 3 = 378 + 4 = 382

Thus the next term is:

382 × 3 = 1146 + 5 = **1151**

Hence, the missing term is 1151.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

16, 17, 25, 52, 116, ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is:

16 + 1³ = 16 + 1 = 17

17 + 2³ = 17 + 8 = 25

25 + 3³ = 25 + 27 = 52

52 + 4³ = 52 + 64 = 116

So next is 116 + 5³ = 116 + 125 = **241**

Hence, the missing term is 241.

The pattern followed is in each term 1st alphabet is at a difference of 4 starting from 1 and 3rd alphabet is at a difference of 4 starting from 6 as per their position in English alphabetical series and the middle digit is a sum of 1st and 3rd alphabetical position of alphabets within each term i.e.

A + 4 = E; F + 4 = J and 1 (A) + 6 (F) = 7

questions.question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

BRV, FVZ, JZD, ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is that each subsequent alphabet is 4 places more than the previous alphabet in each term i.e.

B + 4 = F; F + 4 = J; and J + 4 = **N**

R + 4 = V; V + 4 = Z and Z + 4 = **D**

V + 4 = Z; Z + 4 = D; and D + 4 = **H**

Thus **NDH **is the correct answer.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

A + 2 = C; C + 2 = E; E + 2 = G and G + 2 = **I**

F + 2 = H; H + 2 = J; J + 2 = L and L + 2 = **N**

Thus **IN** is the next term.

questions.question:
Arrange the given words in the sequence in which they occur in the dictionary.

1. Grown

2. Grape

3. Grind

4. Gesture

5. Gentle
questions.solution:
The sequence followed is:

The first letter of every word is ‘G’,

Second letter is arranged i.e. ‘e’ and ‘r’ → Gentle, Gesture will be arranged first.

Third letter in Ge__n__tle, Ge__s__ture → ‘n’ and ‘s’ → dictionary order → Gentle, Gesture

Third letter in Gr__o__wn, Gr__a__pe, Gr__i__nd → ‘a’, ‘i’ and ‘o’ → dictionary order → Grape, Grind, Grown

The dictionary sequence is :

G**__e__**ntle, G**__e__**sture, G**__ra__**pe, G**__ri__**nd, G**__ro__**wn

Thus **5 4 2 3 1 **is the answer.

questions.question: If 19 + 4 # 5 = 39 and 21 # 5 + 6 = 111, then 11 + 15 # 5 = ?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is:

If ‘+’ is the first sign then second sign is ‘×’ and vice versa.

19 + 4 # 5 = 39 ⇒ 19 + 4 × 5 = 19 + 20 = 39

21 # 5 + 6 = 111 ⇒ 21 × 5 + 6 = 105 + 6 = 111

Thus, 11 + 15 # 5 ⇒ 11 + 15 × 5 = 11 + 75 = 86

Hence, **86** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements: **

I. No cup is plate.

II. No plate is spoon.

**Conclusions: **

I. No cup is spoon.

II. Some spoon are cups.
questions.solution:
From the given statements the least possible venn diagram is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b832129c9ad0bc09b65f8a16350791e18b4de18c6caaabeb6d13891ad7ad179c.png] 

**Conclusions: **

I. No cup is spoon → False (it’s possible but not definite)

II. Some spoon are cups → False (it’s possible but not definite)

Thus either I or II is true.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** Conditions of either or case

 
• The elements should be same in both the conclusions
 
• Both conclusions should possible but not definitely true.
 
• One of the conclusion should be negative and one of the conclusion should be positive i.e complimentary pair.
 
• Complimentary pairs :

 
• ​some + no and all + some not
 
• Some + Some not and All + no are not Complimentary pair.

questions.question: In a certain code language, "RAIN" is written as "45" and "GOOD" is written as "44". How is "DROP" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
The pattern followed is that in the given word position of each alphabet in English alphabetical order is done and then 3 is added i.e.

RAIN → R (18) + A (1) + I (9) + N (14) = 42 + 3 = 45

GOOD → G (7) + O (15) + O (15) + D (4) = 41 + 3 = 44

Similarly,

DROP → D (4) + R (18) + O (15) + P (16) = 53 + 3 = 56

Thus **56** is the answer.

questions.question: In a row Sanjay is at 11th position from top and 13th from bottom. How many people are there in the row?
questions.solution:
Given, in a row Sanjay is at 11th position from top and 13th from bottom.

Total number of people in row = (Sanjay’s position from top + Sanjay’s position from bottom) - 1 = 11 + 13 - 1 = 24 - 1 = 23

Thus **23** is the answer.

questions.question: P is 4 years older to Q. Q is 7 years younger to R. R is 5 years older to S. S is 8 years younger to T. Who is the youngest?
questions.solution:
Given, P is 4 years older to Q → P = Q + 4

⇒ P > Q

Q is 7 years younger to R → R = Q + 7 thus R = P + 3

⇒ R > P > Q

R is 5 years older to S → R = S + 5 thus P = S + 2 & S = Q + 2

⇒ R > P > S > Q

S is 8 years younger to T → T = S + 8 thus T = R + 3

⇒ T > R > P > S > Q and it is the final arrangement

Thus **Q** is the youngest one.

questions.question: Weight of P is twice that of Q. Weight of Q is half of R. Weight of R is 3 times of T. Weight of T is half of S. The weight of T is greater than the weight of how many persons among P, Q, R and S?
questions.solution:
Given, Weight of P is twice that of Q i.e. P = 2Q

Weight of Q is half of R i.e. R = 2Q

⇒ P = R = 2Q or can say P = R > Q

Weight of R is 3 times of T i.e. R = 3T

⇒ P = R > Q > T

Now, Weight of T is half of S i.e. S = 2T or S > T

Thus it is clear that Weight of T is not greater than any among P, Q, R and S

Thus **zero** is the answer.
